answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before it can bid, with one active job allowed per bond. Agents named juniper, lotus, and violet face the same rule: creating more names creates no free capacity. An attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds for the full period, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere; splitting one bond among fake accounts cannot multiply access.
